title: Combined: Order System
story: You're launching a small online store! Each order has a customer, an amount, and a status that changes over time — from Pending to Shipped to Delivered. You need both a struct AND an enum to model this properly.
why: Real applications combine structs and enums. Structs hold the data, enums represent state — together they model complex, real-world systems.
analogy: An Order is like a package. The struct is the box (with a label and weight), and the enum is the tracking number's status — the box stays the same, but its status moves through the delivery pipeline.
try_it: Add a `Refunded` status to the OrderStatus enum. Write a `refund` method that only works on Delivered orders. Create an order, ship it, deliver it, then refund it — print the result of each step.
tips: Struct fields can be enum types — `status: OrderStatus` is perfectly valid
Guard transitions with if: `if status == OrderStatus.Pending` before changing to Shipped
Return `Bool` from transition methods so callers know if the state change succeeded
common_mistakes: Allowing any transition: Shipping a Cancelled order should fail — always check the current status
Comparing enum values with `==` on the wrong side: `OrderStatus.Pending == status` works, but `status == OrderStatus.Pending` is more readable
Forgetting to update all references when adding a new Status variant — match arms, if checks, and methods all need updating
